items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: But I played most, a lot of the days with Manuel and Freddie and them

ctx.x: I thought some of the other churches had a lot of singing, you know, spirituals and all that in their churches, like the Baptist.

No, you see the bands, Louis in the late days come out with playing the Saints and all that stuff. But the Saints, they played that when it was going to the funeral with a body. They played that very slow moving around, a 4-4 movement going to the funeral. They played that very early in the funeral. Yeah. See? But in the... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...

They played that very slow movement, a 4-4 movement going to the funeral. But in the later years they come out playing it in ragtime style, you know what I mean? We played places in the south, right in Texas. The man said, well we're going to play the sense. They wouldn't let you play it, you'll have to play it as a preacher, let you play it. Like, or the club was a number closer to the hymns. Just a close walk of the gym. Now we didn't play them kind of things. We didn't play nothing like that in our dance hall.…
